title.narrative: Feed the Future Ghana Fisheries Recovery Activity (GFRA)

description.narrative: (Ghana): The fisheries ecosystem is vital for the Ghanaian people's livelihoods and nutrition. The sustainable productivity and profitability of wild fisheries are endangered by inadequate fishing policies, poor fisheries management, and the lack of participatory decision-making by beneficiaries of the fisheries resources in coastal communities. The small pelagic fisheries (sardines, mackerel, and anchovies) are under threat of collapse, with catches having dropped to about 10 percent of the maximum annual yield. The primary causes of this decline include mismanagement and a lack of enforced regulations that have resulted in overfishing, as well as rampant illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing. A collapse will mean the loss of livelihoods of about 10 percent of the country's population (2.5 million people) directly and indirectly involved in the sector. .The GFRA, in close collaboration with the Ministry of Fisheries and Aquaculture Development and the Fisheries Commission, will use FY 2022 funds to promote sustainable and equitable fishing in Ghana to reverse the declining trend of fish resources and enhance the socio-economic conditions of fishing communities in coastal areas. The Activity will integrate research, governance, livelihoods and resource management to mitigate threats and grow this important economical, dietary, and environmental resource. It will also support activities that aim to reduce the risks of child labor and labor trafficking in the fishing sector through awareness-raising, policy change, and improving livelihoods in target communities. Following a vulnerability assessment, GFRA developed a comprehensive GBV strategy that centers on prevention, targeting fishing communities and constituents to raise public awareness. GFRA will develop complementary materials and roll-out extensive social and behavior change communication interventions for engendering anti-GBV actions... .
